entries.title: Ezekiel 12:2
segments: It is not from the want of means to know God's will that sinners perish, but from unwillingness to use the means which he furnishes them.  Their ignorance is voluntary and inexcusable.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:3
segments: Stuff for removing; literally, "equipments for exile," such as the king and his princes will presently prepare in their flight from Jerusalem,

. 
 
When one method of admonition fails, we must employ others; not intermitting our efforts to reclaim and save sinners, so long as God prolongs to them the day of grace.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:5
segments: Dig thou through the wall; to represent the flight of the king and his princes.  They fled "by night, by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king's garden,"
, doubtless by opening a passage there that had been kept closed during the siege.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:6
segments: In the twilight; in the darkness of night.  See note on

. 
 
  Cover thy face; as a sign of mourning and humiliation.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:13
segments: My net--will I spread upon him; God's net was the army of the Chaldees, which pursued after him and overtook him.
Bring him to Babylon--yet shall he not see it; remarkably fulfilled in the case of Zedekiah, whose eyes were put out before he was carried to Babylon.

Zedekiah enjoyed the faithful instructions of Jeremiah, but he would not listen to them, and therefore all the calamities which the prophet had foretold came upon him.  Led in chains to Babylon with his eyes put out, he became a sad and awful example of the end of those who harden themselves against God's reproofs.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:14
segments: When God is against a sinner, all his human confidences fail him.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:16
segments: May declare all their abominations; the abonimations of their brethren whom God has destroyed, and on account of which they themselves have been carried captive, that thus the heathen may understand the reason of their destruction.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:22
segments:
The days are prolonged; the days for executing the judgments threatened by the prophets. 
 
  Faileth; proves false.  From God's delay they take encouragement to disbelieve his threatenings.

vv 22-28. 
 
God delays the execution of his threatenings, that men may have time for repentance; but they take occasion from this to harden themselves in unbelief and rebellion to their destruction.

entries.title: Ezekiel 12:24
segments: Vain vision--flattering divination; the flatteries of the false prophets were the chief cause why the predictions of the true prophets were disregarded.  While God destroys the former, he will fulfil the words of the latter.
